tips.title: Scribing Panel Lines with RB Productions' Panel Line Scriber
tips.text: For deep, consistent panel lines, use RB Productions' Panel Line Scriber. It has interchangeable tips for various line depths. Apply gentle pressure and guide it along the panel line. For best results, scribe after assembly but before painting. With RB Productions, you can achieve realistic panel lines without damaging the model's surface.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning with Iwata's Airbrush Needle Cleaning Kit
tips.text: A clean needle ensures smooth paint flow and prevents clogging. Use Iwata's Airbrush Needle Cleaning Kit to maintain your needle. First, dissolve dried paint with Iwata's needle cleaning solution. Then, scrub gently with the cleaning brush, rinse with water, and dry with the included towel. Repeat until the needle is clean.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya Tape vs Kabuki Tape
tips.text: Tamiya tape is great for large, flat surfaces due to its strong adhesion. Kabuki tape, however, is more flexible and better suited for curves and complex shapes. For best results, use Tamiya tape for flat areas and Kabuki tape for curves. Before applying, clean the surface with alcohol to remove oils. Press firmly to ensure a good seal, and peel slowly at a 45° angle.

tips.title: Using Dental Tools for Detail Work on Eduard Photo-Etch
tips.text: Eduard's photo-etch frets often include tiny, delicate details. For bending and shaping these parts, use dental tools like the KAI Tweezer and KAI Scalpel. Gently grasp the part with the tweezer, then use the scalpel to bend or cut it. Be careful not to apply too much pressure and damage the part.

tips.title: Sanding Stick Progression for Styrene Sheet (Evergreen)
tips.text: To prepare Evergreen styrene sheet for use, start with a coarse sanding stick to remove the shiny surface and any imperfections. Follow up with a medium to smooth out the surface, then finish with a fine to achieve a glass-like smoothness. Always sand in the direction of the grain and use light, steady pressure. Finally, wipe the sheet with a damp cloth to remove dust.
